# Quantum Group Memory Laws

Research record by Ruge Lin on full real-deformation symmetry projection, spatial spin memory, and physical local erasure.
Canonical repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Group-Memory-Laws
Sister: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Permutation-Noise-Limits

## Scientific question and notation

Use the ordinary physical trace on an open spin-half chain. Pi_r projects onto the whole represented quantum-group star-algebra, including generator products. In the physical-erasure account, r>1 is fixed finite real deformation, p in (0,1) is independent receiver-flagged physical erasure probability, and n is chain length. Older spatial-memory pages write q=r and L=n. Do not confuse deformation with erasure probability.

The complete channel is E_p^tensor n composed with Pi_r, with the stationary projection supplied. Every call transmits one whole n-site block. The two-way quantum capacity has a positive size-independent achievable rate 1-h2(p/2) and a finite upper bound C(r,p), uniform in n, arbitrary encoders, reference inputs and adaptive LOCC. The sharp finite-r capacity is not claimed. A two-site achieved rate R2(r,p) strictly exceeds the exact r=1 two-site benchmark at r>1,p in (0,1), so deformation changes finite-block capacities while preserving a size-independent ceiling.

## Spatial memory retains its own hypotheses

M_(L,i)(q)=2^-L ||Pi_q(X_i)||_HS^2 is the complete symmetry contribution to local Pauli autocorrelation. At q=1 it equals 1/L everywhere. At fixed finite q>1, either end has tanh(log q)/sqrt(2*pi*L)+O_q(L^-1). At fixed q>q0=2.0810189966... and i/L approaching an interior fraction x, the bulk equals K(q)F(x)L^-2[1+o(1)]. The ratio to the center tends F(x)/F(1/2), independent of q in that proved domain. q0 is a sufficient proof threshold, not a physical transition. End and bulk contributions vanish with size; the limits are not uniform near q=1 or boundaries. Keep fixed-distance, fixed-interior and weak-deformation limits separate.

A symmetry-preserving isolated Hamiltonian's finite-size time average is at least M and may have additional invariant information. The specified unrecorded bond-kick dynamics attains the full projection at fixed finite size; its gap scaling is unknown. An actual finite-time implementation needs a separate reference-stable channel approximation and mixing-time account.

## Sister relationship and attribution

Quantum Group Memory Laws owns the physical finite-deformation maps, estimator, all-sector ceiling proof and original spatial laws. Quantum Permutation Noise Limits owns the ordinary-permutation/symmetric-loss reduction, exact r=1 erasure capacities and replacement-noise conclusions. Its exact flagged formula tends -log2(p). That exact formula is not transferred to finite r. Reciprocal accounts retain essential models and conclusions while the full finite-r proof has one home here.

Full commutant projection, representation theory, q-Dicke tools, stationary strong-symmetry mechanisms, symmetric-loss resources, reverse hashing and adaptive squashed-entanglement converse are inherited and cited. The new operational step is the finite-r path-uniform environment estimate and its direct application to the full projected channel. Do not infer communication capacity from local autocorrelation, identify a global algebra isomorphism with physical-loss equivalence, or use an infinite-deformation generator limit as a finite-r theorem.

## Learning and evidence

The one educational anchor is John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~watrous/TQI/. The project bridge supplies quantum-group and estimator steps absent from the textbook. Other primary references remain scholarly proof inputs.

The original 79-file spatial handoff, five nested manifests, license, scientific assertions and canonical reports are preserved. The 24 original groups and four complementary foundation groups check finite identities and evaluations. New checks independently compare physical CG amplitudes, conditional loss maps, all-word/all-flag estimator laws and representative arbitrary-prior posteriors. Finite checker success is not a proof certificate, exact capacity formula, priority guarantee or mixing-time result. Read AGENTS.md before maintenance.

Useful search phrases: quantum group physical erasure capacity; finite deformation two-way quantum capacity ceiling; full symmetry algebra physical multiplicity trace; first erased mismatch Clebsch Gordan; quantum group spin chain boundary bulk memory; quantum group stationary projection local loss; physical embedding symmetric loss Choi spectrum.
